merger_name: Australian Venue Co – assets of 318 Little Collins Street, Melbourne (also known as The Carson)
merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Ltd (**AVC**) proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of the licensed hospitality business intending to trade as The Carson in Victoria, from Datre Pty Ltd (**the Vendor**), including the exclusive right to carry on the business in succession of the Vendor under the benefit of a new lease, pursuant to an asset sale agreement (**the Acquisition**).

For the past 5 years, 318 Little Collins Street, Melbourne has been operating as a small ground-floor retail and food arcade with largely independent tenants offering a limited range of food and beverage options. A major redevelopment was proposed in 2020 to refurbish the existing late-1960s building by adding a large hospitality space and rooftop.

The Carson will be a contemporary, beverage-led rooftop bar and restaurant operating under a Late Night On-Premises Licence located at 318 Little Collins Street, Melbourne. It is expected to open and commence trading in December 2026.

AVC is a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Limited which operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants. AVC’s venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that, if the Acquisition were put into effect, the notification
thresholds would likely be met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market, based on the
information provided. It considers that the Acquisition warrants
consideration through the notification process, including via further
information gathering and consultation with third parties. This may
include a focus on:
a. the extent of horizontal overlap in the Melbourne CBD once
The Carson is operational, noting Australian Venue Co owns
several similar venues in the Melbourne CBD area
b. the extent to which Australian Venue Co is likely to be
constrained by alternative suppliers of dining, function and
on-premises liquor services, particularly at large-format retail
hospitality venues, in the Melbourne CBD area post-
acquisition
c. the extent to which Australian Venue Co’s competitors could
acquire similar assets.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
